summary: Set 130 Session 1 of 3, 'The reader that refuses to guess'. The set's spec was a RESERVED, explicitly-unauthored stub, so it was authored in full before registration and its premise re-derived against the live store rather than inherited: the stub assumed the hard part was reading an undocumented store, but the store is stable (schema_version 6, 17k+ rows) and the real gap is a JOIN KEY that is captured and dropped twice -- cli_transport.py:1073/:1108 reads each routed child's sessionId into transport metadata and metrics.record_call() has no parameter for it, while COPILOT_AGENT_SESSION_ID sits in the seat environment unread. That reframing turned the stub's two sessions into three (read / record / report), journaled under goal-over-letter. It also falsified the stub's claim that routed cost is 'correctly $0.00' on a seat: Set 118 S1's five routed rounds recorded $0.0000 against 866.4 credits ($8.66). SHIPPED: ai_router/docs/seat-cost.md names the three measurements -- routed_api (Direct-API, priced, correct today), routed_seat (routed calls over the Copilot CLI transport, real spend currently reported as $0.00 with billed_usage_unavailable: true) and orchestrator_seat (the conversation that runs the session) -- and states the rule that outlives the set: any report showing one must say which it is showing and name what it could not measure. ai_router/seat_cost.py resolves the store, self-checks its shape BEFORE trusting it (pinned schema_version, required columns), sums total_nano_aiu over an EXPLICIT set of conversation ids, and returns a component-separated CostReport whose absent answer is a named status with credits=None -- never 0.0 -- and whose total exists only when every component was measured. Three traps found by measurement, not by reading: (T4) immutable=1 silently skips the WAL and undercounts a live store, measured at one instant as 17,035 vs 17,036 events and 156.5 vs 168.0 credits; (T5) a session cannot measure its own closing turns, which is why Set 118 recorded $42.67 where the store now reads $47.43; (T6) a time window cannot attribute, because Set 118 S1's wall-clock window also contains 1,277.2 credits of Set 129's conversation. 24 falsifiers, every one planted into a real store and PROVED to fire: planting immutable=1 into the reader failed two tests (behavioural + structural) and planting the rejected spelling into the doc failed a third; all plants reverted. Set 118 S1 re-priced end to end with the shipped tool: $47.43 seat + $8.66 routed = $56.10 against $42.67 recorded and $0.0000 routed.

reason.specifics: Session 2 records the join keys this session proved are missing -- COPILOT_AGENT_SESSION_ID into the session record at registration (APPENDING, because start_session is idempotent and is re-run after a context reset) and the routed child's sessionId onto each metrics row. Its inputs are exactly this session's findings: which key is captured where, why record_call drops it, why attribution must be by id and never by clock, and the additive-null convention Sets 078/084/109 established for metrics columns. Rebuilding that is expensive and carrying it is free. The verifier must remain a non-anthropic provider, as it was here.

notes: COST OF THIS SESSION, measured with the tool this session shipped -- the first time the repo has been able to state it: orchestrator seat 3,050.2 credits ($30.50, 164 turns) + routed calls over the seat 551.3 credits ($5.51, 62 turns across 4 verification rounds, 1 preflight probe and 12 catalog-refresh probes) = 3,601.5 credits ($36.01). Direct-API routed cost is not_applicable. THE TOTAL IS A LOWER BOUND and is labelled one by the tool itself: the turns that author this disposition, commit and close are not in the store yet (trap T5 -- the same effect that made Set 118's $42.67 read $47.43 later). Every routed round in this session reported cost: $0.0000, which is the defect the set exists to fix. || VERIFICATION: 5 rounds. Discovery (fan-out 2, gpt-5.5, lenses spec-conformance + failure-scenario) -> 1 Major: the spec's prose named the measurements routed_call_cost / routed_seat_cost / orchestrator_seat_cost while the code shipped routed_api / routed_seat / orchestrator_seat. Accepted, not disputed, and Major on merit -- those strings are the to_dict() wire keys Session 3's disposition.cost consumes, so ambiguity now becomes a three-surface schema drift later (L-064-8). Short names won (they sit under a 'cost' parent where the suffix stutters); the JUDGMENT criterion was converted into two mechanical tests. Supplementary -> clean. remediation-review -> VERIFIED, fix accepted. Then the guidance/ceiling change triggered a further delta review -> 1 Major (runs of record staled by the config edit), whose executable criterion now passes (exit 0, all three suites fresh and green). Final remediation-review -> VERIFIED, 2 fixes accepted, 0 rejected. || TWO DISCLOSURES A REVIEWER SHOULD CHECK HARDEST. (1) PLAYWRIGHT'S RUN OF RECORD IS A COMPOSITE AND WAS NOT RE-RUN AFTER THE FINAL CONFIG EDIT. The declared 4-worker command ran all 31 specs: 30 passed, 1 failed -- vsix-first-run-walkthrough.spec.ts, which loses a fixed 300s budget for a REAL venv + network pip install against 3 concurrent Electron instances; it passed standalone in 43.6s, the identical adjudication Set 118 recorded. Operator ruled that serial fallback is a return to the pre-parallelism baseline and NOT a verification reduction, and that re-running 30 already-green specs buys no coverage. Later, the ceiling edit staled all three runs by path prefix; pytest was re-run in full (4,398 passed / 9 skipped, 600s) because it is the suite that actually asserts the guidance ceilings, mocha was re-run because it costs 43s, and Playwright was re-recorded on the 03:57 evidence because the entire intervening delta is two integers under guidance.preload plus comments -- non-reachability SHOWN, not asserted: zero occurrences of preload/ceiling_tokens/ceilingTokens anywhere in tools/dabbler-ai-orchestration/src, zero references to router-config in src/test/playwright. All four rulings are operator-attested in decisions.jsonl. (2) THE SPEC AND TWO FIGURES WERE EDITED MID-SESSION. spec.md was authored this session (the stub is at b5e5e364); two prose figures were then corrected from 866.5 cr / $8.67 to the exact 866.4 / $8.66 after the tool showed the first pair had been summed from values already rounded to one decimal. decisions.jsonl still carries the superseded figure and was deliberately NOT rewritten -- it is an append-only record of what was decided when. || NEW GUIDANCE: 'Practicality outranks rule-perfectionism' landed in project-guidance.md under explicit operator authorization to raise the ceiling (3,499 -> 3,930; total 12,200 -> 12,600), raised TO FIT the measurement in the pattern Sets 128 S2/S3 established, to be ratcheted back down by Set 121. It carries both worked cases and the line it must not cross: a different ROUTE to the same evidence, never less evidence. || BOOKKEEPING: activity-log.json carries two stray step rows keyed measurementsNamed / plantedStoreCaught -- the spec's Progress keys were used as step keys before the seeded plan keys were noticed; the plan rows were then reconciled correctly and the strays are left as honest history rather than hand-edited out. ai_router/copilot-catalog.lock was refreshed mid-session (pinned 1.0.79 vs live 1.0.80, fail-closed refusal; 11/18 models confirmed) -- mechanical, not a deliverable, and it cost 63.3 credits ($0.63) that nothing but this session's own new tool can see. || RESIDUAL FOR STEP 9, owned by no set: 'covers' is a PATH PREFIX, so a comment-only or unrelated-key edit to a large shared config stales every suite covering its directory. Set 129 made suites declare their inputs; the next refinement is per-key or per-file granularity for shared configuration. Also unowned since Set 117 was cancelled: a durable flake-quarantine mechanism that records an isolated re-run under a DISTINCT, non-silent outcome rather than a clean green. || CHECKLIST ADVISORY, DISCLOSED RATHER THAN WAIVED (same shape as Set 118 S1): close_preflight reports 5 transitions that left a record with no matching post. Four are operator-stops (value-trade-off) and one is the last-logged-step. The checklist WAS posted at session start, before the first operator brief, before the long-running suite, and before this close. The four unposted ones are mid-conversation operator RULINGS -- the operator interjected with a correction rather than answering a posed question -- so the window for a post-before-the-transition did not exist to be used, and the gate matches a post recorded AFTER the decision is journaled. A window already passed cannot be re-entered and the sanctioned exit is an operator-attested waiver, which is not self-authorizable -- so the rows are left unmet and named here instead. Advisory: it does not refuse the close. Worth raising at Step 9 alongside Set 118's identical observation: the constitution says 'post before the brief', but an operator-initiated ruling has no brief to precede, and the gate currently counts it the same as a missed post.
